title: Comparison of strict and enhanced system operation models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below have $\ell$ invertible and use small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For each scheme $W$, set $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the ordinary category of $B_{W,n}$-module systems with quotient-linear transitions and $D(\mathscr S_W)$ its unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Let $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion and $p:Z\to Y$ a morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the ringed sequence sites [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], let $J_j^{\mathrm{str}}$ be exact extension by zero and let $S_p^{\mathrm{str}}=Rp_{*,\bullet}$ be the total right derived functor of levelwise $p_*$ on the whole system category. Write $e_n$ for evaluation at level $n$, $\tau^M_{m,n}:e_mM\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}e_nM$ ($m\geq n$) for the transitions of a system $M$ and $t^M_{m,n}$ for their extension-form adjoints, and $U_Y$ for termwise restriction of scalars along $\widehat R_Y\to B_{Y,n}$ to strict $\widehat R_Y$-module towers. Let $b_{m,n}$ be the coefficient mate of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for the direct image along $p$. For $M\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ put $T_n(M)=\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}j_!e_nM\in D(\widehat R_Y)$, and for $m\geq n$ give these objects the transition $T_m(M)\to T_n(M)$ equal to $\operatorname{Res}_m$ of the transpose, under $-\otimes^L_{B_{Y,m}}B_{Y,n}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$, of
$$Rp_{*,n}\bigl(t^{N}_{m,n}\bigr)\circ b_{m,n,N_m},\qquad N=J_j^{\mathrm{str}}M,$$
where the system $N$ has the levelwise transitions $j_!(\tau^M_{m,n})$; here $\operatorname{Res}_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_n$. Then for every $M\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ there are natural isomorphisms in $D(\widehat R_Y)$
$$\Theta_{M,n}:\operatorname{ev}_n\bigl(U_Y S_p^{\mathrm{str}}J_j^{\mathrm{str}}M\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_n(M)\qquad(n\geq1),$$
each the canonical evaluation identification $\operatorname{ev}_nU_Y=\operatorname{Res}_ne_n$ followed by $e_nS_p^{\mathrm{str}}\cong Rp_{*,n}e_n$ and $e_nJ_j^{\mathrm{str}}=j_!e_n$, and they carry every transition of the tower $U_YS_p^{\mathrm{str}}J_j^{\mathrm{str}}M$ to the transition of $(T_n(M))_n$ just defined. Thus $\Theta_M=(\Theta_{M,n})_n$ is an isomorphism of whole towers of objects of $D(\widehat R_Y)$. The family is compatible with the units and counits of the open and direct-image adjunctions, natural for every derived morphism of systems, and constructed before taking any inverse limit.

proof.text: The ringed sequence site realizes the ordinary category $\mathscr S_W$ as module sheaves with componentwise exactness, and its evaluation functors are the vertical evaluations described in [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Thus the notation $D(\mathscr S_W)$, $e_n$, and the whole-system direct image $S_p^{\mathrm{str}}$ in the statement refer to the actual ordinary system category; no separate section category is introduced.

source.place: Clause (3), second paragraph: ordinary levelwise compact-support operations assembled into a system before the derived limit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] to the morphism of small pro-etale sites $p_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Its coefficient hypothesis holds: [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] gives ring isomorphisms $p^{-1}B_{Y,n}\cong B_{Z,n}$, and they commute with the quotient maps because both composites send a constant section $a\in A_m$ to its image in $A_n$, which determines a map of constant ring sheaves. The exact inverse image on systems is $V=p^{-1}_\bullet$, the levelwise module direct image has total right derived functor $G=Rp_{*,\bullet}=S_p^{\mathrm{str}}$, and the node supplies natural identifications $e_nG\cong Rp_{*,n}e_n$ compatible with units, counits and transition maps. Its transition clause says that, in extension form, the transitions of $GN$ are $Rp_{*,n}(t^N_{m,n})\circ b_{m,n,N_m}$ with $b_{m,n}$ the specified mate, not a separately chosen level map.

source.place: Clause (3), second paragraph: ordinary levelwise compact-support operations assembled into a system before the derived limit.

proof.text: For the open immersion, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the localization $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}/X$ and $B_{Z,n}|_X$ with $B_{X,n}$, so [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] gives exact $j_!\dashv j^*$ at each level. These extensions commute with restriction along $B_{Z,m}\to B_{Z,n}$, since both leave the underlying additive sheaf unchanged, so applying $j_!$ to every component and every transition $\tau^M_{m,n}$ is the exact system functor $J_j^{\mathrm{str}}$ of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], which acts on derived categories with the ordinary level adjunctions. Being exact and computed termwise, $e_nJ_j^{\mathrm{str}}=j_!e_n$, and the system $N=J_j^{\mathrm{str}}M$ has transitions $j_!(\tau^M_{m,n})$; its extension-form transitions $t^N_{m,n}$ are their adjoints. Combining with step 2 gives the canonical identification $e_nS_p^{\mathrm{str}}J_j^{\mathrm{str}}M\cong Rp_{*,n}j_!e_nM$.

source.place: Clause (3), second paragraph: ordinary levelwise compact-support operations assembled into a system before the derived limit.

proof.text: The identifications of steps 2--3 are natural in $M$. By the transition clause of step 2 applied to $N=J_j^{\mathrm{str}}M$, the extension-form transition of $S_p^{\mathrm{str}}N$ from $m$ to $n$ is carried by these identifications to $Rp_{*,n}(t^N_{m,n})\circ b_{m,n,N_m}$; its restriction-form transition is the transpose under $-\otimes^L_{B_{Y,m}}B_{Y,n}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$, because the two forms of a transition correspond under that adjunction (as in the definition of the reduction maps $t_{m,n}$ in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]). Applying the exact restriction $\operatorname{Res}_m$ and $\operatorname{Res}_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}=\operatorname{Res}_n$ gives exactly the transition of $(T_n(M))_n$ in the statement. Therefore the levelwise identifications carry the transitions of the tower to the displayed ones.

source.place: Clause (3), second paragraph: ordinary levelwise compact-support operations assembled into a system before the derived limit.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars along $\widehat R_Y\to(B_{Y,n})_n$ is exact on the whole system category [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], computed termwise. The exact-functor derived factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] computes $U_Y$ on derived objects and morphisms termwise, so $\operatorname{ev}_nU_Y=\operatorname{Res}_ne_n$ on derived systems, compatibly with transitions. Composing with steps 3--4 gives the isomorphisms $\Theta_{M,n}$ and their compatibility with transitions, i.e. the whole-tower isomorphism $\Theta_M$, natural for every derived system morphism because every identification used is a natural isomorphism of functors.

source.place: Clause (3), second paragraph: ordinary levelwise compact-support operations assembled into a system before the derived limit.

proof.text: The units and counits in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] are the componentwise adjunction maps for $p^{-1}_\bullet\dashv Rp_{*,\bullet}$ and for $j_!\dashv j^*$. Since the evaluation and transition identifications above are the ones supplied by that node, their mate formulas and the corresponding unit/counit identities are carried by $\Theta_M$ to the displayed levelwise formulas. This verifies the claimed compatibility before any inverse limit is taken.
